clue.text: Orlando tips uranium (unknown quantity) in drink

indicators.note: in says the next pieces sit inside the pair taken from Orlando
the tips of a word are its first and last letters, here those of Orlando

parts.note: U is the chemical symbol for uranium
in algebra an unknown quantity is written as x, y or z; here Z

explanation.surface: Someone called Orlando pours a drink spiked with a mysterious dose of uranium.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an aniseed-flavoured Greek spirit, so it is a kind of drink.

clue.text: They separate the good from the bad, Enigmatist and his ilk

definitions.text: They separate the good from the bad
definitions.meaning: a riddle is a coarse sieve, so those who riddle sift good material from waste
Enigmatist is a Guardian crossword setter, and setters pose riddles for a living

explanation.surface: Puzzle setters such as Enigmatist are sorters of good from bad.
explanation.walkthrough: This puzzle's clues each name a fellow Guardian setter; Enigmatist is one, and a riddle is also a large sieve for soil or grain.
explanation.definitionFit: A riddle is a coarse sieve, and riddle-posers include crossword compilers, giving two senses of one plural noun.

clue.text: Something vulgarly dull after Quantum, not specific

indicators.note: after places the word for dull behind the word for quantum

parts.note: taken as a common noun rather than the setter's name, a quantum is an amount or sum
matt or mat means dull, without shine

explanation.surface: A setter called Quantum is accused of a dull, vague clue for something.
explanation.walkthrough: Quantum is a Guardian setter; 'not specific' tells you to read the word generally, as an amount. The answer is northern English dialect for 'something'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a dialect or colloquial pronunciation of something, which 'vulgarly' signals.

clue.text: Clot, daft as brush, Tom

indicators.note: daft means crazy, so the letters of the next words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Calling Tom a clot who is daft as a brush, the British phrase for very silly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daft as a brush' is a British idiom for very foolish, which makes 'Clot' (a fool) look like a character judgement.
explanation.definitionFit: A blood clot that forms inside a vessel is the medical term given here.

clue.text: Flexible machinery etc contains one

indicators.note: contains says the word for machinery holds the next piece

parts.note: plant means industrial machinery and equipment
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A versatile set of machines includes a single unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bending easily is flexible; the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Discouraged? Shed/Gordius cooked fish

indicators.note: shed says the letters of the setter's name are discarded from the first word
cooked means the remaining letters are prepared afresh, rearranged

explanation.surface: A downcast setter, Gordius, sheds his gloom and cooks fish.
explanation.walkthrough: Gordius is a Guardian setter. Strike G, O, R, D, I, U, S from DISCOURAGED to leave C, A, E, D, then 'cooked' rearranges them.
explanation.definitionFit: A small freshwater fish of the carp family, found in European rivers.

clue.text: Incandescent satellite, commandeered by Rufus, reversed mostly

indicators.note: the satellite is seized and held inside the reworked name
most of the name is turned round: its first three letters run backwards while the last two stay

parts.note: Io is one of Jupiter's moons

explanation.surface: A glowing moon is hijacked by someone called Rufus, who has mostly turned back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversed mostly' turns only the first three letters of Rufus round, leaving the last two in place; the moon then sits inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Incandescent is used figuratively for white-hot with rage, which matches very angry.

clue.text: Araucaria's Life-force Bank: secure and electronic

definitions.note: Araucaria's means Araucaria is, so the clue says what the tree genus is

parts.note: chi or qi is the vital force in Chinese philosophy
to bank an aircraft is to lean or tilt it
to pin is to fasten or secure
E is a standard abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail

explanation.surface: Araucaria, the late setter, made a list of life-force, banking, security and electronics.
explanation.walkthrough: Araucaria was a famous Guardian setter, named after the monkey-puzzle tree genus; 'Araucaria's' reads as 'Araucaria is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The monkey-puzzle tree, genus Araucaria, is native to Chile, hence this common name.

clue.text: Smith's predecessor to make Logodaedalus news

definitions.meaning: Logodaedalus is a Guardian setter whose name means a cunning artificer of ..., a wordsmith; the needed ... comes before smith

explanation.surface: A setter called Logodaedalus is to take over from a Mr Smith, according to reports.
explanation.walkthrough: Logodaedalus is Greek-derived for 'word-craftsman'; the first definition wants the word that goes before 'smith' to give that.
explanation.definitionFit: Word can mean news or tidings, as in 'any word from her?', and it precedes smith in wordsmith.

clue.text: Appliance of mechanics principally associated with Brummie — old students beware getting out of line!

indicators.note: principally means first, so take the opening letter of mechanics

parts.note: Brummie is this puzzle's setter, so the setter refers to himself as I

indicators.note: the warning word gets the line placed inside it

parts.note: cave, Latin for beware, was public-school slang shouted as a warning that a master was coming
a row is a line

explanation.surface: Brummie's appliance comes with a warning to former pupils about stepping out of line.
explanation.walkthrough: Brummie is the setter, so 'Brummie' gives I. Cave (pronounced KAY-vee) was the old schoolboy cry of 'look out'; 'getting' puts the line inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A microwave oven is a common kitchen appliance.

clue.text: Chifonie clone, different league involved — an honorary title only

indicators.note: involved says the next piece is wrapped up inside the jumble
different says the letters of the two words are made into something else

explanation.surface: Chifonie and a clone in a different league pursue a merely honorary rank.
explanation.walkthrough: Chifonie is a Guardian setter. 'different' rearranges the two words, and 'involved' wraps that jumble around the abbreviation for league.
explanation.definitionFit: This military rank is an honorary title, often held by royals as nominal head of a regiment.

clue.text: Wedge foreign article in scanning equipment

indicators.note: in places the article inside the scanner's name

parts.note: a CAT scanner is a medical imaging machine
le is the French word for the

explanation.surface: Someone wedges a strange item into a medical scanner.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleat is a wedge-shaped piece of wood or metal used to secure ropes or prevent slipping.

clue.text: Like a drink offered by one having flutter in the "Parrot"

indicators.note: in says the two pieces sit inside the bird

parts.note: a lory is a brightly coloured parrot
I is the Roman numeral for one
to bat, as in batting eyelids, is to flutter

explanation.surface: A drink is offered by someone who has a gamble in a pub called the Parrot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flutter' suggests a small bet, but here it means batting the eyelids.
explanation.definitionFit: A libation is a drink poured out as an offering, and this adjective describes such offerings.

clue.text: Move at will: Rover might follow in a vehicle

definitions.text: Rover might follow in a vehicle
definitions.meaning: the ... Rover is a British four-wheel-drive car, Rover coming after the first word in its name

explanation.surface: A dog named Rover roams freely and trails after a car.
explanation.walkthrough: Range Rover is a well-known British luxury off-road vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Ranging means wandering at will, and it is the word preceding Rover in a car's name.

clue.text: Bent tibias — sex rejected and abandoned

indicators.note: abandoned says the turned letters are dropped from tibias
rejected means the word for sex is sent back, read backwards

parts.note: it is a coy word for sex or sex appeal

explanation.surface: Bow-legged shinbones are rejected for sex and abandoned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns IT into TI, which 'abandoned' strips from the front of TIBIAS.
explanation.definitionFit: A bent can mean an inclination or leaning, the same as a bias.

clue.text: Pasquale's hogging card partner and dance partner of Paul

indicators.note: hogging means keeping something to oneself, so the first piece holds the partner

parts.note: Joe Pasquale is a British comedian, so Pasquale's reads as Joe's
in bridge the players are North, South, East and West; North partners South

explanation.surface: A setter called Pasquale greedily keeps his bridge partner and Paul's dancing partner.
explanation.walkthrough: Pasquale looks like the Guardian setter, but Joe Pasquale is a British TV comedian. The Paul Jones is a party mixer dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The Paul Jones is a ballroom mixer dance, so the second word accompanies Paul in its name.

clue.text: Janus, teaming with Losey (poles apart), might produce "Tango"

indicators.note: might produce says the pieces can be reworked to make the answer
apart says the poles are separated off from the setter's name

parts.note: N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: The setter Janus teams up with the film-maker Losey to produce a tango film.
explanation.walkthrough: Janus is a Guardian setter; Joseph Losey a film director. Removing N and S from JANUS leaves JAU, which is shuffled with LOSEY.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacob Gade's 'Jalousie', known in English by this name, is one of the most famous tangos.

clue.text: See 8
Insert pike into seeds and sort of screw

indicators.note: insert says one piece is put into another
into names the seeds as the receiving piece

parts.note: pips are fruit seeds
a pike is a peaked hill in the English Lake District, as in Scafell Pike

explanation.surface: An instruction to stuff a fish among seeds, and a kind of screw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pike' suggests a fish, but in northern England it is a hilltop. A Phillips screw has a cross-shaped slot.
explanation.definitionFit: The Phillips screw, with its cross-head recess, is a named type of screw.

clue.text: The very last in the queue despite expectations?

definitions.text: The very last in the queue
definitions.meaning: the person standing behind everyone else in a line
in spite of what was thought

explanation.surface: The final person in a queue is there against expectations.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in spite of what was expected, and literally describes being behind everyone.

clue.text: Parent dealt in ecstasy

indicators.note: dealt like cards, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A parent is handing out ecstasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ecstasy' suggests the drug, but the definition means rapturous.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in rapture or transported with delight is to be in ecstasy.

clue.text: Maybe Bunthorne's in musical entertainment as an Irish saint?

definitions.meaning: Gilbert and Sullivan's operetta Patience is subtitled 'Bunthorne's ...'
Saint ..., or Brigid of Kildare, is a patron saint of Ireland

explanation.surface: A setter called Bunthorne might appear in a musical as an Irish saint.
explanation.walkthrough: Bunthorne is a Guardian setter, but also the poet in Gilbert and Sullivan's comic opera Patience, or Bunthorne's Bride.
explanation.definitionFit: St Bride (Brigid) is an Irish saint, and in the operetta the title character is Bunthorne's betrothed.

clue.text: Bathroom fixtures, dead expensive, finally in pieces

indicators.note: in places the final letters inside the word for pieces

parts.note: bits are pieces

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of dead and of expensive

explanation.surface: Costly bathroom fittings arrive in pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: These low washbasins are fixed plumbing items found in some bathrooms.

clue.text: Whipped round with pile to be laundered

indicators.note: laundered means cleaned and reworked, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A carpet's pile is beaten and sent round to the laundry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whipped' suggests beating, but it is slang for stolen; 'with' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Whipped is informal for stolen, and the answer means taken dishonestly.

clue.text: Maybe Auster's other Guardian pseudonym

definitions.meaning: his other name, the given one
the name under which John Halpern sets Guardian cryptics

explanation.surface: A novelist named Auster may have another Guardian pen name.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both the novelist Auster's first name and the byline of a Guardian crossword setter.

clue.text: Vein on Latin lines

indicators.note: on places the lines after the abbreviation, as is usual in down-and-across conventions

parts.note: an ode is a poem, lines of verse

explanation.surface: A vein of meaning in some Latin verse.
explanation.definitionFit: A lode is a vein of metal ore in rock.

clue.text: Pop! Audreus rallied round Lendl's lead, producing a double service

indicators.note: round says the jumble goes around the next letter
rallied suggests regrouping, so the letters are rearranged
a word's lead is its first letter

explanation.surface: The setter Audreus watches tennis rallies around Ivan Lendl, who serves a double fault.
explanation.walkthrough: Audreus is a Guardian setter; Ivan Lendl a tennis champion. Shuffling POP and AUDREUS, then adding L from Lendl, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with two uses serves twice over, a double service in a functional sense.

clue.text: See 23
One ideally situated to muddle on with Taupi

indicators.note: to muddle is to mix up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone well placed proceeds to confuse the setter Taupi.
explanation.walkthrough: Taupi is a Guardian setter; 'with' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A utopian is an idealist, someone living in an imagined perfect place.
